campaign.scriptedWorkflowsAndInjectionCorpus: run in every shard beside its seeded episodes

mutants.defect: A read tool that joins the model's path onto the workspace folder without refusing traversal, absolute paths or a symbolic link that leaves the workspace (R-30, I-07 on the read side)
Tools sorted by a priority number and cut at the profile's cap, so a small profile or an excluded tool left an editing agent with part of its tool set and no word about it (R-36)
A command listed in the repository's `.onyx/config.json` `terminalAllowlist` runs with no approval dialog (Cursor red flag 2; Claude B2; Codex; R-01, R-02)
A "Run for This Session" or "Always Run" answer: one approval of a command text runs every later invocation of that text, whatever changed underneath it (R-03, R-04)
The approval dialog shows a whitespace-collapsed copy of the command while the original bytes are dispatched, so what the user approved is not what runs
A `verificationTask` named in the repository's `.onyx/config.json` runs a workspace task after a tool-using run with no approval for that run

A regex pass over the command string with no egress, persistence or interpreter category: fifteen of the sixteen bypass commands of the launch audit, every exfiltration shape among them, reach the approval prompt with no warning (Claude H1; R-06)
The terminal service kept everything a command printed after its sixth timeline note for as long as the command ran: `pendingChunk` grew without bound (Codex N11; R-18)
A command the agent proposed was started with the whole environment of the process that started it, credentials included (Codex N11; I-10)
The directory a terminal call named was ignored (`cwdHint`), so a command meant for a subdirectory ran in the workspace root (Codex N11)
Nothing killed a running command when its window closed or the runtime service was disposed: `dispose()` aborted HTTP operations and left `_runningCommands` alone (Codex N11; R-18)

The diagnostics export rewrote only the `value` of prompt message parts; tool parameters, note labels and reasons, command text and output, paths and the model's reply went into a "redacted" bundle as they were (Codex N1; R-20)
A stream whose body ended without a finish reason or `[DONE]` was reported as done; the run was journaled as completed (Codex N12; R-19)
Tool arguments were handed to the tool without being checked against its schema: a terminal call with `timeoutSeconds: "forever"` ran with the default timeout (R-28)
A request that never produced a byte was waited on with no deadline, so the run never ended on its own (Codex N12; R-19)
Chat requests carried no `max_tokens`: nothing reserved room for the reply or bounded it (Claude H6; Codex N9; R-16)
Tool results accumulated across turns with no re-budgeting, so the prompt outgrew the context window (Claude H6; Codex N9; R-16)
A loopback address was taken to mean local inference: a model the runtime reports as cloud-backed was used like any other, with nothing said (Claude H7; DEC-04; R-17)
No handling of `<think>` tags: a reasoning model's thinking was its reply, so a reply that ended mid-thought was shown as an answer and the run completed (Cursor 3.1; R-26)
Any reply opening with a code fence was withheld as a possible tool call until it was 4,000 characters long or finished, so a code answer showed nothing while it streamed (Claude H5; R-27)
A constrained turn showed nothing until its whole JSON envelope had arrived, so a long answer appeared all at once at the end (R-28, optional part)
The loop took its harness decisions inline and hashed a record of some of them into the trace; the hash named no configuration a second run could be given (R-44)

Whatever core's tool registry holds reaches the model: `runTask`, `createAndRunTask`, a rename that writes without staging, the browser tools, MCP and extension tools, each with core's own confirmations or none (Claude H2; R-05)
A note the model asks to remember is stored at once and added to every later prompt, so text injected through a file or a command's output steers later runs (I-14, R-59)

A SEARCH text that is not in the file was still placed: after trimming each line and re-indenting the replacement, or by its first line alone when that was unique, which replaced lines the model never quoted (Claude H3; R-07, R-33)
A SEARCH text that occurs more than once was placed at the first of them instead of refused as ambiguous (Claude H4; DEC-07; R-08)

A hunk was accepted by its place in the list: after the user changed the lines of the first hunk, accepting what was shown as the first hunk applied the one that had moved into its place (Codex N2; R-12)
A proposal of any size was diffed and staged: nothing refused one above the documented bound before the quadratic line diff ran (C9; R-38)
The write side never asked where a file really is: an edit to a symbolic link that leaves the workspace was staged, and accepting it wrote outside the workspace (R-30, write side)
A certificate that says "seen this turn" of an edit whose quoted text the model had not been sent: the one observation a certificate adds, reported as true whatever happened (R-46)
A deleted line was replaced by nothing and its line break stayed, so an accepted deletion left an empty line and the buffer was not the proposal (Codex N3; R-13)
An inline edit wrote the model's reply into the buffer and reviewed it afterwards, so model-authored text was in the file, and in what an autosave wrote, before any accept (R-34)
Stop set a status and released the pause gate; the inference token and the running tool were not cancelled, so the turn in flight still ran its command (Codex N5; R-15)
A terminal status could be replaced: Stop set `cancelled`, and the loop then recorded `completed` when the stream ended (Codex N5; R-15)
A run the user paused and did not resume never ended on its own: a pause had no time budget (Codex N5; I-03)
Verification ran when a tool-using turn ended, before anything was accepted: a run that had only staged an edit reported "no new problems" of files that did not hold it (Codex N6; R-21)
Generic: an edit that is staged is applied to the file at once, with no accept. Not an audited defect: the guard I-01 stands on, taken away for the agent's own edit path
Generic: every command the model asks for is run without a dialog. Not an audited defect: the guard I-02 stands on, taken away whatever the configuration says
Generic: a run is never given a terminal status. Not an audited defect: the guard I-03 stands on

Generic: the write side resolves a path by joining it onto the folder, so a parent-directory segment or an absolute path stages a file outside the workspace. Not an audited defect: the two guards I-07 stands on for writes, both. With the path check alone removed, the check of where the file really is still refuses the edit

Generic: tools are dispatched and nothing is written to the run's journal about it. Not an audited defect: the guard I-12 stands on. No mutant covered I-12 before L12, and its checker compared only the rig's own events; the journal side was added with this mutant
